votes.quote: they've caught a real bug in `globToRegex.ts`. The spec says a trailing `/` after `**` should be consumed by the `**` (so `**/yarn.lock` matches `yarn.lock` and `a/**/b` matches `a/b`), but the current implementation just emits `.*` for `**` and leaves the following `/` as a separate literal, so those cases don't match.
